findings: CROSS_QUESTION: q5 option C's subordinate clause ('when it leaves cancelled sailings out of the count') asserts that the clause excludes cancelled sailings, which directly contradicts and eliminates option D here.

ENTAILMENT: q5 options A and D both presuppose that punctuality is scored against the booked timetable — that presupposition is what makes 'lengthening the timetable' a way to keep the payment — and that is exactly what option A states.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: altitude — A is the only option that says what the payment turns on; B, C and D are incidental facts about it, so A answers the stem's 'what are we told about the payment' at the level the stem invites.

justification: I reach A at roughly 55 percent. D is eliminable outright from q5C's clause, and the whole-text framing in q5 corroborates A's mechanism. What I could not infer is whether B or C is true — the six-year payment history in C and the contract-drafting date in B are both unverifiable from stems, so I am narrowing on A rather than confirming it.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: q3 option C ('what first began to stretch the gap between one departure and the next') together with q5 options A and D (timetable lengthened, journeys longer) makes option B's 'seventy minutes apart, as they still do' incoherent with the text's premise. B is eliminable without the passage.

CROSS_QUESTION: q1 option C ('gone unpaid in one quarter of the past six years') implies measurement spans about six years and so began well after 2005, which corroborates D rather than A. The channel narrows the field but then splits it.
CALIBRATION: student-available, form and cross-reading only.
justification: I narrowed 4 to 2 (A and D) at roughly 45 percent on A, choosing A because Cottam reads as the operator's defender and 'the 2005 timetable was already tighter than the crossing took' is the stronger defence. I could not tell whether the text's defence is that the old timetable was unrealistic (A) or that no one was measuring yet (D); both are live and q1C mildly favours D.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: q5 options A and D establish that the text's spine is a lengthened timetable and longer journeys. Option C is the only option that supplies a cause for that lengthening, so thematic centrality selects it.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: altitude — C connects the withdrawal to the text's main variable; A, B and D are local chronology or attribution claims that do no work in the argument the other stems reveal.

CROSS_QUESTION: q1 option B ('written into the contract when the second boat was withdrawn') supplies an independent date anchor for the withdrawal that interacts with option A here, but the two cancel rather than resolve — at most one can be true and I cannot tell which.
CALIBRATION: student-available. 'Pick the option that carries the text's main causal claim' is standard test-wiseness.
justification: I reach C at roughly 45 percent purely on thematic centrality — it is the option that would matter to the argument the other four stems sketch. I could not infer the actual chronology (A), the reason for withdrawal (B), or the departure arithmetic (D); those need the passage. This is a real but non-decisive channel.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: the four options form a complete 2x2 over two binaries — accept her numbers? accept her cause? — A no/no, B yes/no, C yes/yes, D no/yes. A complete matrix is good design (no odd-one-out), but fixing either variable halves the field.

CROSS_QUESTION: q5 option D frames the text as 'the disagreement over what connects the two', i.e. a causal dispute over facts both sides accept. That fixes 'accept her numbers' to yes and 'accept her cause' to no — precisely option B.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: register — A's rhetorical doubling ('her minutes show little and her explanation still less') is markedly more dismissive than the other three and reads as the throwaway.
CALIBRATION: student-available in its first move (spot the 2x2, drop the sneering option); the q5-to-q4 transfer is a more advanced move.
justification: I reach B at roughly 45 percent, arriving via q5 rather than via this question. Note the circularity: q4 and q5 are mutually informative, so a student who knows neither cannot bootstrap — the channel only pays if you have independently settled the main idea. I could not discriminate B from C on this question's own terms.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and D are a minimal pair differing on exactly one variable. Both assert punctuality maintained/improved plus lengthened journeys; A asserts the causal link as settled ('has kept its punctuality payment BY lengthening the timetable'), D leaves it open ('the disagreement over what connects the two').

CROSS_QUESTION: q4 asks about the writer's attitude to Cattermay's argument and its option axis is explicitly 'the cause she assigns them', which establishes that the causal link is contested in the text. A main-idea key cannot settle what another stem treats as disputed, so A falls and the hedged twin D stands.

CROSS_QUESTION: q3 ('what is implied about the withdrawal of the relief boat') puts a second candidate cause for the lengthening on the table, confirming the text's dispute is causal rather than evidentiary — which is what rules out B's 'a dispute over which of them to believe'.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: B mischaracterises the relation. An improved punctuality figure and longer measured journeys do not 'point in opposite directions' — they are simultaneously true, which is the text's actual point. A main-idea key would not misstate its own subject.

REPAIR CHECK (altitude): CLOSED. A, B and D are all genuine whole-text readings sharing the same two-clause 'thesis plus consequence' shape. C is whole-text in form ('whether a clause should go into a new contract unchanged') though anchored on one contractual detail. The round-1 channel 'only the key sits at whole-text altitude' no longer exists.

REPAIR CHECK (limb corroboration by other stems): PARTIAL. Corroboration is now distributed rather than unique — A's limbs are named by q1 (the payment) and q2/q3 (the lengthening); B's by q1 (a reliability figure) and q4 (doubting her numbers); D's by q1, q2/q3 and q4. No single option is uniquely corroborated any more, which is a real improvement. The residual leak is the A/D minimal pair resolved by q4's cause axis — a narrower and different channel than round 1's, but still sufficient.

CALIBRATION: partly student-available. The A-versus-D move ('two options say the same thing, one hedges the cause, another question shows the cause is disputed — take the hedge') is form-only test-wiseness a strong candidate could run. The B-versus-D discrimination requires seeing that the two figures are compatible rather than contradictory, which a Swedish 18-year-old likely lacks.
justification: I land on D at roughly 65 percent without the passage, so by the stated threshold this is a kill — though a marginal one, and I want the channel change on record. The repair genuinely worked on the axis it targeted: all four options are now credible whole-text candidates and the corroboration is spread across three of them. What replaced it is a minimal-pair channel: A and D differ only in whether the causal link is asserted or left open, and q4's existence — a whole question devoted to whether the writer accepts her cause — settles that the text treats it as open. B then falls on its own mischaracterisation. What I could not infer: any number, any name's role, or which of q4's four attitude cells is true — only that the dispute is causal, which is all this question needed.

findings: REPAIR CHECK (off-dimension eliminability): SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED. A (drawn through the middle), B (levelled by eye once the water was on) and C (a gentler fall than the ground below) all directly answer 'how the main channel was to be laid'. D is the weakest fit — it describes the channel's terminus and function rather than its laying — but it is not blatantly off-dimension the way two options were in round 2.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: in Swedish översilning / flood-meadow practice the carrier channel is deliberately given LESS fall than the natural slope so the water rises to the brim and spills evenly along its whole length. That is option C, verbatim. This is the main reason I am above chance.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: register — B's 'efter ögonmått' (by eye) reads as too slapdash for an engineered specification, a mild eliminator on form alone.

CALIBRATION: NOT student-available. The hydraulic principle behind C is specialist agricultural-history knowledge a Swedish 18-year-old almost certainly lacks. And on a flat myr, A ('through the middle, spreading to both sides') is a genuinely real design too — which is what holds me at medium rather than high.
justification: I reach C at roughly 50 percent, and honestly almost all of that is domain knowledge rather than anything the item leaks. The off-dimension channel that was flagged in round 2 is closed: three of four options answer the question actually asked. A student without the översilning background would be near chance here, which is the calibration point that matters.

findings: REPAIR CHECK (MIRRORED_TWIN / reversed causal arrow): CLOSED. I cannot identify a 'broken' option without the passage. A (silt and dissolved nutrients carried in by the water) and B (oxygen in the running water speeding peat breakdown and releasing nutrients) are two genuinely different mechanisms — allochthonous input versus in-situ mineralisation — not one another with the arrow reversed, and both are real and coherent standing alone. C (moisture retention against summer drying) and D (winter ice shielding roots from frost) are likewise independently coherent and both are documented benefits of the practice. No option is incoherent alone.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: B is the most mechanistically specific option (a three-step causal chain), the classic length-and-specificity tell, which is essentially my whole reason for picking it.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (weak): a myr is wet by definition, which slightly discounts C's moisture argument; and the stem's hedge 'framställs i texten som' hints the text may prefer a non-obvious mechanism over the folk 'gödslande slam' answer (A). Both signals are soft and neither is reliable.

CALIBRATION: the residual is form-only (option specificity) and so student-available in principle, but weak. At roughly 35 percent against a 25 percent base rate this target sits on the pass/flag boundary; I flag rather than pass only because the specificity tell is nameable.
justification: This is the target I was asked to judge afresh for the reversed-arrow problem, and my answer is that I cannot tell which option is 'broken' — because none of them is. All four are mechanisms a person could believe on their own. I pick B on option texture alone and I would not defend it; A is equally live and is the historically dominant explanation. The round-2 channel is closed.

findings: REPAIR CHECK (off-dimension eliminability): CLOSED. All four options are authorial-purpose shaped ('för att ...') and all four concern the 1858 agreement's content or evidential role. None is eliminable for failing to answer what the stem asks.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: a 2/2 verb split survives — A and C are merely informative ('för att ange'), B and D are demonstrative ('för att visa'). Authorial-purpose keys normally key to the demonstrative member, which halves the field to B and D.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: the canonical content of a 19th-century Swedish multi-farm water agreement is the turn order for the water (turordning) — option D. That, on top of the verb split, is what puts me above chance. Note that C (dagsverken apportionment) is equally canonical content for such a document, which is why D is not a confident pick.

CROSS_QUESTION (weak): q4's options A and C treat 'källmaterial' and 'kartor och handlingar' as the contested ground between the two researchers, which frames the 1858 agreement as demonstrative evidence and reinforces the visa-over-ange narrowing.
CALIBRATION: the verb split is form-only and student-available; the D-over-B choice needs period knowledge a Swedish 18-year-old likely lacks.
justification: I reach D at roughly 40 percent. The off-dimension problem from round 2 is genuinely fixed — every option is a plausible reason an author would cite the agreement. What remains is a phrasing artefact (ange versus visa) that is probably incidental to the generator's style rather than designed, plus domain knowledge. I could not infer what the agreement actually contained.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and C sit on one axis — is the dispute about which sources suffice (A) or about how the same sources are read (C)? A reader who takes that axis to be the question's real subject narrows to those two at 50 percent.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: a second 2/2 form split — A and B both open 'Den gäller i första hand ...' (what the dispute is about), C and D both open 'Den beror på / bottnar i ...' (what causes it). The parallel phrasing marks the axes for the reader before any content is considered.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: odd-one-out — D is the only option grounding the dispute in a difference of scale between the two researchers' studies, and its 'många fler socknar' magnitude claim reads as the throwaway.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C is the accommodating both-sides reading that 'vad kan man dra för slutsats om oenigheten' stems usually key to, which is most of my reason for picking it.
CALIBRATION: student-available. All four signals here are form — parallel phrasing, odd-one-out, and the both-sides preference — with no domain knowledge required.
justification: I reach C at roughly 45 percent on form alone, which is the uncomfortable part: nothing in my reasoning touched the actual content of the disagreement. I could not infer who Pärlhage and Nolvide are, what they disagree about, or whether the text even reports a methodological versus interpretive split. This is a generic test-wiseness pull toward the accommodating option rather than a leak of this item's content.

findings: REPAIR CHECK (contradictories on one variable): CLOSED, though contradiction remains. The colour axis now carries THREE pairwise-incompatible options — A (varying colour card to card), B (uniform blue laid over the plate's clouds), D (left white on most) — with C (clouds added on nine cards) on a separate axis and logically compatible with any of the three. Under a one-true-answer assumption a 3+1 exclusivity cluster carries no information: if the cluster holds the key with probability 0.75, each member sits at 0.25, exactly the base rate. The round-2 2+2 pair, by contrast, concentrated 0.5 on two options. Going three-way neutralises the leak.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (insufficient): C is the only option with a bare count ('nio av korten') and the only one off the colour axis — a weak odd-one-out signal that points in no determinate direction. D's 'de flesta' is a comparable quantifier tell on the other side, so the two cancel.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: no discrimination available. Leaving skies white, laying flat blue straight over a plate's clouds, and varying the tint between runs are all documented practices in early hand-coloured photographic postcards. Period knowledge ranks none of them above the others.
CALIBRATION: n/a — no channel reaches usable strength, so there is nothing for a student to exploit.
justification: I put B at about 32 percent against a 25 percent base rate and I do not treat that as beating chance. My pick rests on nothing but option texture — 'plåtens moln' reads like a close-study finding rather than a manufactured claim — which is not a channel I would stand behind. The repair target is closed for a specific structural reason worth recording: three-way exclusivity is informationally inert where two-way exclusivity is not.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: dimension-match — the stem asks what shows a postmark says little about when the PICTURE WAS TAKEN, but B and C only stretch the printing-to-posting interval and say nothing about the taking-to-printing one. A sharp reader narrows to A (older pictures bought in) and D (the same motif reprinted for years).

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: a second, cruder narrowing — C and D are the two duration mechanisms while A and B are provenance/ownership claims. D is the only option that survives BOTH narrowings, and that convergence is what puts me above chance.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A is the odd one out on the temporal axis (it is as much about place as about time) and B is the most convoluted chain, so both read as the weaker pair on form alone.

CALIBRATION: student-available. The channel is pure dimension-matching against the stem's own wording — no knowledge of postcard publishing is needed to run it, only care about what 'när bilden togs' actually asks.
justification: I reach D at roughly 45 percent. All four options are valid mechanisms for widening the postmark-to-photograph gap, which is good construction — there is no free elimination on plausibility. The leak is that two of the four do not reach the specific gap the stem names, and D is the option that both natural narrowing strategies converge on. I could not infer which mechanism the passage actually asserts; C in particular remains a strong live candidate.

findings: RULE 15 (a) ONE-WAY LEAK: NONE FOUND. No option in q1 carries a clause asserting anything q2 tests — nothing about printing dates, editions, shop shelf-life or provenance appears in the sky options. Symmetrically, no option in q2 says anything about the sky or the colouring. q1 option B's 'plåtens moln' does establish that a photographic plate underlies the cards, but that is shared setting, not an answer to q2.

RULE 15 (a) SOFT BIDIRECTIONAL LINK (not a one-way leak): q1 option A (colour varying from card to card) and q2 option D (the same motif printed in new editions for many years) mutually raise each other's plausibility, since separate print runs would be separately coloured. Because it runs in both directions and is probabilistic rather than assertive, it does not hand over an answer.

RULE 15 (b) SYMMETRIC VOUCHING: PRESENT BUT WEAK. Both option sets are drawn from one small factual world — a single publisher's postcard series, a photographic plate, hand-colouring, print runs, shops, postmarks, other towns, other publishers. Reading both stems reconstructs the passage's subject (dating and describing a local postcard series) more fully than either alone. But no member of either set asserts a fact that answers the other, so the vouching raises situational understanding without transferring an answer.

JOINT STEMS-ONLY SOLVABILITY: not materially above the per-question level. q1 stays at roughly base rate (about 32 percent on B) and q2 at roughly 45 percent on D. The pairing adds no independent leverage; q2's channel is internal dimension-matching, not anything q1 supplies.

DOES ANSWERING ONE SHIFT THE OTHER: yes, but only marginally. Committing q1=A would lift q2=D via the multiple-print-runs link; committing q1=B (a uniform, systematic colouring practice applied to one plate) mildly lowers it. I estimate the shift at 5 to 8 percentage points — not decisive, and it cannot be used to bootstrap either answer, since q1 is itself unanswerable blind.
CALIBRATION: nothing here is student-exploitable. Extracting even the 5-to-8-point shift requires an explicit model of postcard production that no candidate would build under time pressure.
justification: Analysed as a pair, las-b20-003 is close to clean. There is no one-way leak in either direction, and the only cross-talk is a soft, symmetric plausibility link between q1A and q2D that runs through a shared production model rather than through any asserted fact. The two questions do share one small factual world, which is the flag: a two-question unit drawn this tightly from one subject inevitably vouches for itself at the level of setting. I record it as a flag rather than a pass because the vouching is real and worth tracking if more questions are ever added to this unit, not because it makes either question answerable.
